name: Gaian regulation — stable only above the critical fidelity c/b
summary: For a regulating trait with private return fidelity × benefit and cost c, reports the critical fidelity c/b, the selection gradient and the stability eigenvalue, and checks that regulation is stable exactly when fidelity exceeds c/b.

reconciliation.note: The record's status in the canon catalog is 'working' (working corpus, not spine-admitted). The file compiles with standard axioms only in the 2026-11-13 compile census; the classification must be reconciled before admission.

inputs.name: fidelity
inputs.help: Fidelity ρ_f: the share of a regulating act's benefit that returns to the actor.

derived.name: selection_gradient
derived.description: ρ_f·b − c (positive: individual selection favours regulation)

derived.name: stability_eigenvalue
derived.description: c − ρ_f·b (negative: the regulating state is stable)

conclusion.check: (stability_eigenvalue >= 0 or approx_le(critical_fidelity, fidelity)) and (critical_fidelity >= fidelity or approx_le(stability_eigenvalue, 0, cost))

scope: Theorem function: the Lean hypotheses and conclusion restated as checks over supplied real values (IEEE double arithmetic; conclusion compared with a 1e-9 relative tolerance).
boundary: This is conditional mathematics about the supplied values only: it reports whether the Lean theorem's hypotheses hold for them and, if so, the conclusion the theorem guarantees. It does not establish empirical validity, a real-world magnitude, Viridis review, certification, a credit, or a registry determination. It says nothing about whether the Earth system regulates itself: fidelity, benefit and cost are inputs of a stylized selection model.
